Winnipeg, Manitoba--(Newsfile Corp. - November 23, 2026) - Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. (NASDAQ: FNUC) ("Frontier"), a nuclear fuel cycle company, announces that on November 18, 2026, it received written notice from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") that Frontier was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) because it had not timely filed its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (the "Annual Report") with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"). Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) requires listed companies to timely file all required periodic financial reports with the SEC.

The Nasdaq notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of Frontier's securities. Nasdaq has given Frontier 60 calendar days, until January 18, 2027, to submit a plan to regain compliance. Frontier expects to file the Annual Report before the January 18, 2027 deadline and will submit a compliance plan by that deadline if required.

If Nasdaq accepts a compliance plan submitted by Frontier, it may grant an exception of up to 180 calendar days from the filing due date, through May 17, 2027, for Frontier to regain compliance. There can be no assurance that Nasdaq will accept any plan submitted by Frontier or that Frontier will regain compliance within any exception period granted. If Nasdaq declines to accept the plan, Frontier may appeal the decision to a Nasdaq Hearings Panel.

Frontier is issuing this release pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(b). Nasdaq advised Frontier that it will be added to Nasdaq's public list of non-compliant companies beginning five business days after the date of the notice. Nasdaq will also distribute a non-compliance indicator through its market data network and make it available to third-party market data providers.

About Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc.

Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. is focused on building a U.S.-based nuclear fuel cycle platform through uranium exploration and development assets, together with targeted investments in Ubaryon Pty. Ltd., a private Australian company developing next generation enrichment technology, and Kadmos Energy Services LLC, a private U.S. company developing small modular light water reactors. Frontier continues to evaluate opportunities in the nuclear fuel cycle that align with its long-term strategic objectives.

For more information, visit: www.frontiernuclear.com.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Inc. ("Tuya" or the "Company") (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391), a global leading AI cloud platform service provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the declaration of a cash dividend.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Total revenue was US$98.6 million, up approximately 19.5% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$82.5 million).

  • Platform-as-a-service ("PaaS") revenue was US$70.1 million, up approximately 18.3% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$59.2 million).

  • AI application & others revenue was US$13.6 million, up approximately 18.6% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$11.5 million).

  • Smart home & robot product revenue was US$15.0 million, up approximately 26.7% year-over-year (3Q2025: US$11.8 million).

  • Overall gross margin was 45.8%, down 2.5 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 48.3%). Gross margin of PaaS was 45.7% (3Q2025: 48.8%).

  • Operating margin was 9.0%, up 4.4 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 4.6%). Non-GAAP operating margin was 9.5% (3Q2025: 10.8%).

  • Net margin was 18.8%, improved by 0.6 percentage points year-over-year (3Q2025: 18.2%). Non-GAAP net margin was 19.3% (3Q2025: 24.4%).

  • Net profit was US$18.5 million (3Q2025: US$15.0 million). Non-GAAP net profit was US$19.1 million (3Q2025: US$20.1 million).

  • Net cash generated from operating activities was US$12.7 million (3Q2025: US$30.0 million).

  • Total cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and treasury securities recorded as short-term and long-term investments were US$971.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to US$1,017.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

For further information on the non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

Third Quarter 2026 Operating Highlights

  • Premium PaaS customers[1] for the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2026 were 331 (3Q2025: 280). In the third quarter of 2026, the Company's premium PaaS customers contributed approximately 89.6% of its PaaS revenue (3Q2025: approximately 88.0%).

  • Registered AI developers were over 2,180,000 as of September 30, 2026, up approximately 21.0% from approximately 1,801,000 developers as of December 31, 2025.
  1. The Company defines a premium PaaS customer as a customer as of a given date that contributed more than US$100,000 of PaaS revenue during the immediately preceding 12-month period.

Mr. Xueji (Jerry) Wang, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Tuya, commented, "In the third quarter, opportunities and challenges coexisted in the global consumer electronics industry. On the one hand, AI-native hardware continued to move from concept toward deployment at scale. New categories such as companion robots and AI toys rose rapidly, becoming a new engine for industry growth, which fully demonstrated that users' new demands for hardware in the AI era have begun to emerge. On the other hand, upstream component costs such as memory chips were still rising, and demand in traditional categories also faced pressure. Against this backdrop, we still maintained solid growth, with total revenue increasing by 19.5% year over year to US$98.6 million. The growth rate further accelerated compared to the second quarter, and we achieved year-over-year growth for the 13th consecutive quarter. In particular, PaaS revenue grew by 18.3% year over year, reflecting the continued increase in penetration of smart products across different regions and categories.

We continued to fully embrace AI and accelerated the promotion of ecosystem deployment. During the quarter, shipments of new AI-native categories grew by over 400% year over year. We debuted the AI home companion robot Doova at IFA in Berlin and the Global Digital Trade Expo. With the AI life assistant Hey Tuya as a core entry point, we integrated the three major application ecosystems of AI Home, AI Robot, and AI Energy, as well as the full-stack Matter combo solution. At the same time, subscription businesses such as door lock value-added services and pet cloud storage developed steadily, driving a continuous increase in the proportion of recurring revenue. Regarding developer tools, following Tuya Cobuilder, we launched the AI-native no-code application development platform Tuya AI Coding this quarter, extending developer tools from hardware development to application development. Looking ahead, we will focus on the three major scenarios mentioned above to promote large-scale shipments and the commercialization of AI-native hardware such as companion robots, pet care devices, and home energy management devices, and continue to improve the developer toolchain, Agent orchestration, and commercialization capabilities."

Mr. Yi (Alex) Yang, Director and Chief Financial Officer of Tuya, added, "In the third quarter, all three business segments delivered year-over-year revenue growth, with total revenue increasing by 19.5% year over year to US$98.6 million. As a foundation for our growth, the PaaS business saw its revenue increase by 18.3% year over year to US$70.1 million; Premium PaaS customers contributed approximately 89.6% of the PaaS revenue, and the core customer base remained stable. Smart home & robot product revenue grew by 26.7% year over year to US$15.0 million, primarily benefiting from growth in demand for categories such as AI audio and video, AI companion toys, and energy. AI application & others revenue increased by 18.6% year over year to US$13.6 million, primarily driven by the growth in cloud services, AI video cloud storage, and AI value-added services."

Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

REVENUE

Total revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 19.5% to US$98.6 million from US$82.5 million in the same period of 2025.

  • PaaS revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 18.3% to US$70.1 million from US$59.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increasing demand compared with the same period of 2025 and the Company's strategic focus on customer needs and product enhancements, despite the disruptions in the international business environment due to tariff-related headwinds since April 2025. Our core customer base remained stable.

  • AI application & others revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 18.6% to US$13.6 million from US$11.5 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to an increase in revenue from cloud-based services. During the quarter, the Company remained committed to offering recurring value-added services with AI application functions.

  • Smart home & robot product revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 26.7% to US$15.0 million from US$11.8 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to growing customer demands.

GROSS PROFIT AND GROSS MARGIN

Total gross profit in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 13.6% to US$45.2 million from US$39.8 million in the same period of 2025. The gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 45.8%, compared to 48.3% in the same period of 2025.

  • PaaS gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 45.7%, compared to 48.8% in the same period of 2025, partly attributable to recent price fluctuations in the semiconductor supply chain.

  • AI application & others gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 75.7%, compared to 70.8% in the same period of 2025.

  • Smart home & robot product gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 19.3%, compared to 23.8% in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin fluctuated primarily due to changes in product and solution mix, as well as fluctuations in semiconductor supply-chain pricing. As an AI developer platform with a rich ecosystem of smart devices and applications, the Company remains focused on AI offering with compelling value propositions while maintaining economic efficiency.

OPERATING EXPENSES

Operating expenses increased by 0.8% to US$36.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 from US$36.0 million in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased by 15.9% to US$35.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 from US$30.9 million in the same period of 2025. For further information on the non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

  • Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$25.0 million, up 9.7% from US$22.8 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to i) higher employee-related cost and outsourced labor cost of US$1.8 million, ii) higher third-party cloud service fees of US$0.4 million, iii) partially offset by lower share-based compensation expenses of US$0.8 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized. Non-GAAP adjusted research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$24.6 million, compared to US$21.7 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$9.3 million, up 16.9% from US$8.0 million in the same period of 2025, primarily because of i) higher employee-related cost of US$0.9 million, ii) higher third-party cloud expense of US$0.2 million, iii) partially offset by lower share-based compensation expenses of US$0.4 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized. Non-GAAP adjusted sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$9.3 million, compared to US$7.5 million in the same period of 2025.

  • General and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$5.3 million, down 38.0% from US$8.5 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to i) lower share-based compensation expenses of US$3.4 million as equity incentive awards granted at higher valuations in previous years have been gradually amortized, ii) partially offset by higher employee-related cost of US$0.3 million. Non-GAAP adjusted general and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$5.1 million, compared to US$4.9 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Other operating incomes, net in the third quarter of 2026 was US$3.3 million, primarily due to the receipt of software value-added tax refunds.

PROFIT FROM OPERATIONS AND OPERATING MARGIN

Profit from operations in the third quarter of 2026 was US$8.9 million, compared to US$3.8 million in the same period of 2025. The Company had a non-GAAP profit from operations of US$9.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$8.9 million in the same period of 2025, demonstrating consistent operating profitability and leverage.

Operating margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 9.0%, up 4.4 percentage points from 4.6% in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 9.5%, down 1.3 percentage points from 10.8% in the same period of 2025.

NET PROFIT AND NET MARGIN

Net profit in the third quarter of 2026 was US$18.5 million, an increase of 23.8% from US$15.0 million in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP net profit in the third quarter of 2026 was US$19.1 million, compared to US$20.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Net margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 18.8%, an improvement of 0.6 percentage points from 18.2% in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP net margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 19.3%, compared to 24.4% in the same period of 2025.

BASIC AND DILUTED NET PROFIT PER ADS

Basic and diluted net profit per ADS was US$0.03 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$0.02 in the same period of 2025. Each ADS represents one Class A ordinary share.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net profit per ADS was US$0.03 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to US$0.03 in the same period of 2025.

CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS, TIME DEPOSITS AND TREASURY SECURITIES RECORDED AS SHORT-TERM AND LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS

Cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and treasury securities recorded as short-term and long-term investments were US$971.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to US$1,017.3 million as of December 31, 2025. The Company believes its current cash position is sufficient to meet its current liquidity and working capital needs.

NET CASH GENERATED FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES

Net cash generated from operating activities in the third quarter of 2026 was US$12.7 million, compared to US$30.0 million in the same period of 2025. The net cash generated from operating activities for the third quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to working capital changes in the ordinary course of business.

For further information on non-GAAP financial measures presented above, see the section headed "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

Business Outlook

Currently, innovative AI hardware is in a rapid ramp-up phase, but the overall macroeconomic environment remains complex. On the one hand, AI-native hardware is moving from concept toward deployment at scale, with new categories such as companion robots and AI toys rising rapidly, becoming a new engine for industry growth. On the other hand, upstream component costs such as memory chips continue to rise, demand recovery in certain traditional categories is relatively slow, and uncertainties relating to trade policies and supply chains remain. Performance varies across regions, categories and markets. With the accelerated integration of AI and consumer hardware, Physical AI scenarios are ushering in a broader space for development.

Against this backdrop, we will continue to advance our AI-driven strategy. At the product level, we will focus on three high-potential scenarios, namely AI Home, AI Energy and AI Robot, to promote large-scale shipments and the commercialization of AI-native hardware such as companion robots, home energy management devices, and pet care devices. At the developer platform level, we will continue to improve Tuya Cobuilder, Tuya AI Coding and Agent orchestration capabilities, further lowering the development threshold, and enabling more customers and brands to quickly launch their own AI applications based on the Tuya platform. At the user application level, we will continue to enhance the response efficiency and reliability of Hey Tuya, and advance subscription and value-added services such as AI-powered protection, AI energy saving, pet care, and video understanding, to enhance our renewal and ongoing service capabilities.

Looking ahead, we will maintain disciplined execution, and continuously invest in AI R&D and platform capabilities. We will focus on AI-native applications, Physical AI scenarios, and developer platform construction, leveraging the advantages of our platform, device ecosystem and global developer base to transform AI technology from a tool capability into real and scalable commercial value. At the same time, we also recognize that our future performance may be affected by changes in consumer demand, regional economic conditions, inventory cycles, component and logistics costs, foreign exchange and interest-rate volatility, tariffs and trade-policy adjustments, and broader geopolitical uncertainties.

Declaration of Cash Dividend and Record Date

On November 23, 2026, the Board approved the declaration and distribution of a cash dividend (the "Cash Dividend") of US$0.0570 per ordinary share, or US$0.0570 per ADS, to such holders as at the close of business on January 6, 2027, Hong Kong Time and New York Time, respectively. The aggregate amount of the Cash Dividend will be approximately US$35 million, which is payable in U.S. dollars and in cash, and will be funded by surplus cash and to be paid out from the share premium account of the Company. The determination to make distributions and the amount of such distributions will be made at the discretion of its Board and will be based upon the Company's operations and earnings, including, but not limited to, considerations of the Company's GAAP and Non-GAAP net profits, cash flows, financial conditions and other relevant factors.

In order to qualify for the Cash Dividend, with respect to ordinary shares registered on the Company's Hong Kong share register, all valid documents for the transfers of shares accompanied by the relevant share certificates must be lodged with the Company's Hong Kong share registrar, Computershare Hong Kong Investor Services Limited, at Shops 1712-1716, 17th Floor, Hopewell Centre, 183 Queen's Road East, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, no later than 4:30 p.m. on Wednesday, January 6, 2027, Hong Kong time; and with respect to the ordinary shares registered on the Company's principal share register in the Cayman Islands, all valid documents for the transfers of shares accompanied by the relevant share certificates must be lodged with the Company's principal share registrar, Maples Fund Services (Cayman) Limited, at PO Box 1093, Boundary Hall, Cricket Square, Grand Cayman, KY1-1102, Cayman Islands, no later than 3:30 p.m. on Tuesday, January 5, 2027, Cayman Islands time (due to the time difference between Cayman Islands and Hong Kong). Cash Dividend to be paid to the holders of ADSs issued by the depositary of the ADSs will be subject to the terms of the deposit agreement. The payment date is expected to be on or around January 20, 2027 for holders of ordinary shares and on or around January 27, 2027 for holders of ADSs.

About Tuya Inc.

Tuya Inc. (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391) is a global leading AI cloud platform service provider with a mission to build an AI developer ecosystem and enable everything to be smart. Tuya has pioneered a purpose-built AI cloud platform with cloud and generative AI capabilities that delivers a full suite of offerings, including Platform-as-a-Service, or PaaS, AI application & others and Smart home & robot products for developers of smart device, commercial applications, and industries. Through its AI developer platform, Tuya has activated a vibrant global developer community of brands, OEMs, AI agents, system integrators and independent software vendors to collectively strive for smart solutions ecosystem embodying the principles of green and low-carbon, security, high efficiency, agility, and openness.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

In evaluating the business, the Company considers and uses non-GAAP financial measures, such as non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP profit from operations (including non-GAAP operating margin), non-GAAP net profit (including non-GAAP net margin), and non-GAAP basic and diluted net profit per ADS, as supplemental measures to review and assess its operating performance. The presentation of non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America ("U.S. GAAP"). The Company defines non-GAAP financial measures by excluding the impact of share-based compensation expenses and credit-related impairment/(reversal) of long-term investments from the respective GAAP financial measures. The Company presents the non-GAAP financial measures because they are used by the management to evaluate its operating performance and formulate business plans. The Company also believes that the use of the non-GAAP financial measures facilitates investors' assessment of its operating performance.

2026 Holiday Lineup Includes Santa Visits on Select Dates Dec. 4 – 20, Seasonal Lightings, a Radio City Rockettes Combo Ticket, and Festive Décor

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Empire State Building (ESB), the "World's Most Famous Building," today announced its 2026 holiday celebrations, with festive décor throughout the iconic Observation Deck Experience, a Radio City Rockettes combo ticket, visits from Santa Claus, and screenings of “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York” and “Elf." Movie nights will take place on select dates Dec. 11 – 19 and Santa will visit on select dates Dec. 4 – 20. The seasonal lineup invites New Yorkers and visitors to celebrate the holidays at the #1 Top Attraction in the United States in Tripadvisor’s 2026 Travelers’ Choice Awards: Best of the Best Things to Do.

Santa Claus on the 86th Floor Observation Deck

“There is no better place for holiday activities in NYC than the Empire State Building, where the traditions of the season meet an authentic New York experience,” said Andrew Giancamilli, president of the Empire State Building Observation Deck and brand management. “From our festive décor and holiday movie nights to our world-famous views, we invite guests to celebrate the season at a place that is part of New York’s history and so many visitors’ holiday memories.”

All Dressed Up for the Holidays

The Empire State Building Observation Deck Experience will be decked out in festive holiday décor, which includes a seasonal photo corner on the northeast side of the 86th Floor Observation Deck with the New York City skyline as its backdrop. Visitors can explore the interactive second-floor museum before they head up 1,050 feet above street level to New York City’s highest 360-degree outdoor observation deck–the only observation deck in NYC with outdoor heaters for the winter season. For views from 1,250 feet above street level, guests can add access to the enclosed 102nd Floor Observation Deck, which features floor-to-ceiling windows.

Skyline Views and Holiday High Kicks

Guests can pair a visit to the Empire State Building Observation Deck with the “Christmas Spectacular Starring the Radio City Rockettes” at Radio City Music Hall through a special holiday combo ticket. The package combines the building’s immersive second-floor museum and 86th Floor Observation Deck with a ticket to select performances of the Christmas Spectacular for a day of classic New York City holiday activities.

Combo tickets start at $153 and are available at www.esbnyc.com/buy-tickets/esb-radio-city-rockettes-ticket-bundle.

Holiday Classics Above the City

Fans can celebrate the Empire State Building’s place in holiday movie history with special screenings of “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York” and “Elf,” two festive favorites that star the iconic landmark, on the following dates:

  • “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York”: Dec. 11-12 at 5:15 p.m. and 8:30 p.m., and Dec. 16 at 7:30 p.m.
  • “Elf”: Dec. 17 at 7:30 p.m., and Dec. 18-19 at 5:15 p.m. and 8:30 p.m.

Guests should arrive 45 minutes before their scheduled screening. For tickets and more details, visit www.esbnyc.com/best-nyc-holiday-empire-state-building-observation-deck.

Santa Takes His Wish Lists to New Heights

Families can meet Santa Claus and pose for holiday photos during special appearances at the Empire State Building on the following dates and times:

  • Dec. 4, 11, and 18: 2–4 p.m.
  • Dec. 5, 12, and 19: noon–3 p.m.
  • Dec. 6, 13, and 20: 1–4 p.m.

The visits offer guests a chance to share their holiday wish lists and add a seasonal photo to their tour of the Observation Deck. Tickets are available at https://www.esbnyc.com/buy-tickets.

A Taste of the Holidays

Guests can warm up at Eataly’s pop-up located on the 86th Floor Observation Deck, which features hot chocolate with pistachio, gianduja, or caramel and whipped cream, plus a special ESB hot chocolate with espresso, whipped cream, and chocolate drizzle. Italian treats include filled bomboloni and cannoli, alongside a selection of panini, gelato, and coffee.

Holiday Cheer Around Every Corner

Located steps from Herald Square and Macy’s flagship store, and a short walk from Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park, the Empire State Building offers an ideal stop on a day of holiday shopping and sightseeing in Midtown Manhattan. Guests can pair skyline views with nearby gift shopping, seasonal treats, and beloved New York City holiday traditions.

Holiday Nights, Empire State Lights

The Empire State Building’s iconic tower lights will shine throughout the holiday season with dedicated lightings for Thanksgiving, Chanukah, Christmas, and New Year’s, in addition to the annual holiday music-to-light spectacular.

The tower lighting calendar and updates are available at https://www.esbnyc.com/about/tower-lights. Text CONNECT to 274-16 to receive real-time information about ESB’s tower lightings.

Plan Your Holiday Visit

The Empire State Building is located at 350 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10118. Observation Deck visitors should enter at 20 West 34th Street, between Fifth and Sixth Avenues.

The Observation Deck is open every day, including holidays. Hours for each visit date are available at www.esbnyc.com/visit/hours-of-operation.

Observation Deck tickets start at $46 for the 86th Floor and $81 for access to both the 86th and 102nd floors. Prices vary by visit date and ticket type. For all ticket options, current prices, and reservations, visit https://www.esbnyc.com/buy-tickets.

From its immersive exhibits to its iconic 86th Floor and 102nd Floor Observation Decks, the Empire State Building Observation Deck offers visitors a chance to explore the building’s history, its place in popular culture, and New York City’s best views.

Hi-res holiday imagery can be downloaded here.

About the Empire State Building

The Empire State Building, the "World's Most Famous Building," owned by Empire State Realty Trust, Inc. (NYSE:ESRT), soars 1,454 feet above Midtown Manhattan from base to antenna. The Empire State Building Observation Deck features an all-new experience with a dedicated guest entrance, an interactive museum with nine galleries, and a redesigned 102nd Floor Observation Deck with floor-to-ceiling windows. The journey to the world-famous 86th Floor Observation Deck, the highest 360-degree, open-air observatory with views of New York and beyond, orients visitors for their entire New York City experience and covers everything from the building's iconic history to its current place in pop culture. The Empire State Building Observation Deck welcomes millions of visitors each year and is ranked the #1 Top Attraction in the United States in Tripadvisor's 2026 Travelers' Choice Awards: Best of the Best Things to Do, "America's Favorite Building" by the American Institute of Architects, the world's most popular travel destination by Uber, and the #1 New York City attraction in Lonely Planet's Ultimate Travel List. Since 2011, the building has been fully powered by renewable wind electricity, and its many floors house a diverse array of office tenants such as LinkedIn and Shutterstock, as well as dining options like STATE Grill and Bar, Tacombi, Ghirardelli, and Starbucks. For more information and Empire State Building Observation Deck tickets visit esbnyc.com or follow the building's Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, Weibo, YouTube, or TikTok.

Point of sale and prepaid services revenue grew 15.1% year-over-year while general and administrative expenses declined 15.4%

Completed ClearLine sale during the quarter; GrowthLine opened to partner brands after quarter end

Ended the quarter with $4.7 million in cash and stockholders’ equity of $7.9 million

BARTLETT, Tenn., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SurgePays, Inc. (NASDAQ: SURG) (“SurgePays” or the “Company”), a fintech company that launches and runs wireless brands, today announced its financial results for the third quarter and first nine-month period ended September 30, 2026.

“During the third quarter we strategically focused SurgePays’ business model on our core prepaid wireless and fintech businesses, completing the sale of ClearLine and reporting our first full quarter under the amended AT&T agreement. Third quarter revenue totaled $17.3 million,(1) an increase of 6.5% sequentially, and nine-month revenue totaled $49.5 million, up 21.3% over the same period last year. Our point of sale and prepaid services business grew 15.1% year-over-year, while general and administrative expenses declined 15.4%. With this focus and a stronger balance sheet, we are positioned to grow on infrastructure we have already built. That is how we intend to build value for the Company,” said Brian Cox, Chief Executive Officer of SurgePays.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Revenue of $17.27 million, up 6.5% from $16.20 million in the second quarter of 2026 and down 7.6% from $18.68 million in the third quarter of 2025. Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $49.45 million, up 21.3% from $40.78 million in the prior year period.
  • Point-of-Sale and Prepaid Services segment revenue of $15.10 million, up 15.1% from $13.12 million in the prior year quarter. Nine-month segment revenue of $43.90 million was up 43.2%.
  • Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) segment revenue of $2.08 million, compared with $5.56 million in the prior year quarter. The decrease reflects the pause in new user intake by the Company’s Eligible Telecommunications Carrier following an audit delay in the fourth quarter of 2025, as described in the Company’s Form 10-Q.
  • MVNO segment gross margin improved to (23.1)% from (47.2)%, and the MVNO gross loss narrowed to $0.48 million from $2.63 million. The quarter was the first full quarter under the amended AT&T agreement.
  • Total gross loss of $2.84 million, compared with $2.60 million in the prior year quarter. Point-of-Sale and Prepaid Services gross margin was (16.4)% compared with 0.2%, and the Company expects to focus on improving gross margin in that segment during the remainder of 2026.
  • General and administrative expenses of $3.68 million, down 15.4% from $4.35 million. Nine-month general and administrative expenses of $11.82 million were down 10.1%.
  • Income from operations of $20.65 million, compared with a loss from operations of $6.95 million in the prior year quarter, including the $27.17 million non-cash gain on the sale of the ClearLine platform assets.
  • Net income available to common stockholders of $18.11 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, or $0.41 per basic share and $0.34 per diluted share, which includes a non-cash gain of $27.17 million on the sale of the ClearLine platform assets, compared with a net loss of $7.49 million, or $(0.38) per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Nine-month net income was $7.35 million compared with a net loss of $22.21 million.
  • Net cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 improved to $12.49 million from $17.73 million.
  • Cash and cash equivalents of $4.68 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $1.73 million at December 31, 2025.
  • Total stockholders’ equity was $7.85 million, compared with a stockholders’ deficit of $15.40 million at December 31, 2025.

Third Quarter Operational Highlights

  • Completed the first full quarter under Amendment No. 2 to the AT&T agreement, which replaced the pricing schedule and removed all minimum spend commitments. The Company had no remaining minimum spend commitments under the agreement at September 30, 2026.
  • Formed Redline Wireless Group, LLC in August, a joint venture 51% owned by SurgePays as managing member, to distribute LinkUp Mobile prepaid wireless service through the independent dealer channel of a national wireless master distribution organization.
  • Completed the sale of the ClearLine platform assets on September 10, 2026 to a subsidiary of GPO Plus, Inc. in exchange for 25,000,000 shares of GPO Plus Series D Preferred Stock. In connection with the sale, SurgePays holds a put option giving it the right to sell the Series D Preferred Stock, or the common stock it converts into, for $27.5 million in cash through December 9, 2029. The sale did not affect the Company’s prepaid top-up, fintech transaction processing, MVNO or MVNE operations.
  • Signed a non-binding letter of intent on September 17, 2026 with All Prepaid, LLC, dba LowWeeklyPayments, to form a joint venture, 51% owned by SurgePays, to scale the smartphone rent-to-own program across the SurgePays independent retail dealer network, which has onboarded more than 100 dealers.

Subsequent Events

  • On October 15, 2026, the Company announced that GrowthLine by SurgePays is open to partner brands. GrowthLine supports more than 200,000 subscribers across SurgePays platforms. Partners join under a revenue share agreement or a joint venture in which SurgePays is majority owner and managing member.
  • On October 29, 2026, the Company announced a definitive agreement with IP Mobile, LLC (iPMobile), which will serve as the exclusive rural broadband sales channel partner for GrowthLine. iPMobile expects to bring more than 15 rural broadband brands onto GrowthLine over the next 12 months.
  • On November 3, 2026, the Company announced a prepaid wireless agreement for SurgePays POS with Zulie Venture Inc. dba Etime system, a payments network serving more than 1,000 retail locations. Etime system has committed to at least $48 million in prepaid wireless purchase volume from October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027, a minimum of $4 million a month, and the volume began running in early October. The Company expects SurgePays POS transactions to exceed $10 million per month by the end of 2026.

Preliminary October 2026 Revenue

The Company is also reporting that, based on preliminary, unaudited results, total revenue for October 2026 exceeded $10 million for the month.

“The third quarter was when we changed how SurgePays operates, with new carrier economics, continued growth in point of sale and prepaid services, and a sharper focus after the ClearLine sale. October is our first read on what that business produces, and preliminary revenue above $10 million is an encouraging sign that those changes are working,” said Mr. Cox.

“We see growth trending toward custom branded wireless, and we want a bigger share of it,” added Mr. Cox. “GrowthLine removes the years and cost of building a wireless operation, so our partners can put their entire budget into customer acquisition and add subscribers faster. Those subscribers run on infrastructure we have already built, and we share in the margin on each one, or hold majority ownership in a joint venture, without funding that customer acquisition ourselves. Separately, through the joint venture we are pursuing with LowWeeklyPayments, we intend to scale our smartphone rent-to-own program across our independent dealer network.”

(1)         All numbers herein rounded and approximate.

About SurgePays, Inc.

SurgePays, Inc. (NASDAQ: SURG) is a fintech company that launches and runs wireless brands. Through its GrowthLine platform, SurgePays provides partners with carrier access, technology, payments, customer care, compliance and daily operations from platforms it developed and an operations center and NOC it runs. The Company also owns LinkUp Mobile, its own prepaid wireless brand, and operates SurgePays POS, which handles retail sales and payments for wireless companies at neighborhood stores. SurgePays brings affordable wireless service and prepaid financial products to consumers through partners and neighborhood stores. For more information, please visit www.surgepays.com.

Chan holds a degree in Economics from the University of Calgary, and an MBA from Dalhousie University.

HOUSTON, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Intuitive Machines, Inc. (Nasdaq: LUNR) (“Intuitive Machines”, together with its subsidiaries, the “Company”), a space infrastructure technology and services leader, today announced the successful completion of the preliminary design review for the Stirling Technology spAce Research experimenT (START). The successful review is a key milestone for START, which is being developed by Intuitive Machines in partnership with the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory’s (AFRL) Space Operations via Nuclear Enhanced Technology (SONET) team.


Conceptual rendering of the Stirling Technology spAce Research experimenT (START)

This collaboration between commercial industry and the Department of the Air Force aims to mature compact nuclear power technology toward flight readiness, benefitting America’s national space enterprise. It also advances Intuitive Machines’ strategically important development of space nuclear systems designed to enable longer-duration operations on the Moon and in deep space.

The partnership is part of Intuitive Machines’ previously announced $8.2 million contract extension from the AFRL/RJ to advance compact nuclear power technology toward flight readiness. The program is developing technologies intended to overcome the limitations of solar power and enable longer-duration missions on the Moon and deep space.

“Surviving the lunar night is a fundamental infrastructure challenge we have to solve if we want to operate on the Moon for weeks, months, and eventually years,” said Tim Crain, co-founder and CTO for Intuitive Machines. “Intuitive Machines is advancing space nuclear systems to provide the heat and power capabilities needed to extend mission duration and support sustained operations on the Moon for our customers.”

A lunar night lasts approximately 14 Earth days, creating prolonged periods without sunlight and exposing surface systems to extreme cold. These conditions present a fundamental challenge for spacecraft designed around solar power and batteries and limit how long systems can operate on the lunar surface.

START is designed to demonstrate Stirling power conversion technology in space, converting heat from a radioisotope source into electricity. As part of the AFRL/RJ program, the technology is slated to fly to the International Space Station (ISS) through the ISS National Laboratory in early 2028, using electrical power from the space station to simulate the heat from a radioisotope nuclear source.

Intuitive Machines is a next-generation space infrastructure company delivering integrated capabilities that build mission-critical spacecraft and systems, connect networks, and operate space infrastructure across Earth orbit, cislunar space, and deep space. NORWALK, Conn., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Terex Corporation (NYSE: TEX) ("Terex") today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Aerials segment, including the Genie® brand, to Linamar Corporation (TSX: LNR) ("Linamar") for approximately $1.4 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments.

The Aerials segment designs, manufactures, services and markets aerial work platform equipment and telehandlers as well as their related components and replacement parts sold under the Genie® brand. The transaction includes all assets of the business, including intellectual property, manufacturing footprint and parts and service operations.

The sale is the latest step in Terex's strategic transformation, which has included the 2024 acquisition of the Environmental Solutions Group, the 2025 exit of its Tower and Rough Terrain Cranes businesses, and the merger with REV Group, completed on February 2, 2026. Following the closing of the transaction, Terex will operate three segments: Environmental Solutions, Materials Processing and Specialty Vehicles.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, these three segments generated net sales of approximately $4.3 billion and segment Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $711 million, at a combined Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 16.4% before corporate costs. Year to date Adjusted EBITDA margins were 17.0% for Environmental Solutions, 17.8% for Materials Processing and 15.0% for Specialty Vehicles.

Simon Meester, President and Chief Executive Officer of Terex, commented:

"This agreement is the result of a thorough strategic review of Aerials and delivers on the plan we previously announced, continuing the transformation of our portfolio from cyclical mining and construction markets to a leading position in resilient essential services markets. With this sale, Terex becomes a high mix, low volume specialty equipment manufacturer with steady replacement demand, low capital intensity and strong conversion of earnings into free cash flow. That gives us greater flexibility to invest in the business and deliver more predictable and accretive returns to shareholders over time. Genie has a talented team with a respected position across its markets, and Linamar is a strong long-term owner for the business, its customers and its employees. I want to thank the Aerials team for their contributions to Terex and for their continued commitment through the transition ahead."

Strategic Positioning

  • Leading Specialty Equipment Portfolio. Terex will concentrate on businesses with strong brands serving the emergency vehicle market, waste collection, utilities, infrastructure, recycling and materials processing, with strong synergies across the portfolio.
  • Shift in Mix Toward Low Cyclical Essential Services. Excluding Aerials, first nine months 2026 net sales were approximately 40% Specialty Vehicles (public safety and recreation), 30% Environmental Solutions (waste and utilities) and 30% Materials Processing (infrastructure and recycling).
  • Steady Replacement Demand and $6.2B Backlog ex-Aerials. Terex's businesses serve end markets characterized by steady replacement demand and long-term growth, supported by an extensive manufacturing footprint, primarily within the U.S., and strong backlog providing forward demand planning visibility.
  • Low Capital Intensity and Strong Cash Flow Conversion. The continuing businesses are expected to combine low capital intensity with durable, predictable earnings, driving strong free cash flow conversion.

Transaction Details

Under the terms of the agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the Terex Board of Directors, Linamar will acquire Terex's Aerials business, including the Genie® brand, intellectual property, manufacturing footprint and parts and service operations, for approximately $1.4 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments. The transaction is expected to close in 2027, subject to the receipt of required regulatory approvals and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

Advisors

UBS Investment Bank and Barclays Capital are serving as financial advisors to Terex, and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP is serving as legal counsel.

About Terex

Terex Corporation is a global leader in specialized equipment solutions, serving essential sectors such as emergency services, waste and recycling, utilities, and construction. Our diversified portfolio positions us in resilient, high-demand markets with strong long-term growth potential.

We design and manufacture advanced specialty vehicles—including fire, ambulance, and recreational vehicles—alongside waste collection vehicles, materials processing machinery, mobile elevating work platforms, and equipment for the electric utility industry. Through our global dealer, parts and service network and true value-creating digital solutions, we deliver best-in-class lifecycle support, helping customers maximize return on investment.

With its center of gravity firmly in the United States, anchored by a strong domestic manufacturing footprint and complemented by operations across Europe and Asia Pacific, Terex combines local expertise with global reach to capture opportunities worldwide. Our strategy is clear: exceed customer expectations, invest in innovation, leverage our diversified portfolio, and deliver consistent, profitable growth for our shareholders.

DAVENPORT, Iowa, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Iowa American Water announced today that eligible customers will receive a bill credit beginning Nov. 23, following the company's receipt of additional proceeds from settlements reached with manufacturers of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

The latest distribution includes approximately $667,000 in settlement proceeds and accrued interest. The credit is expected to be approximately $9.72 per eligible customer account. The credit amount appearing on individual customer bills may vary based on eligibility and the number of qualifying accounts at the time the credit is applied. This is the fourth bill credit being issued to Iowa American Water customers as part of the settlement proceeds. Customers previously received credits of $9.58 in August 2026, $32.48 in February 2026, and $10.81 in November 2025.

"We are pleased to return these settlement proceeds directly to our customers," said Brad Nielsen, president of Iowa American Water. "This credit provides a tangible customer benefit while supporting our continued commitment to providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable water service across Iowa."

Customers do not need to take any action to receive the credit. It will be applied automatically to eligible accounts and identified on the bill as a credit resulting from Iowa American Water's receipt of settlement proceeds from PFAS manufacturers.

Iowa American Water participated with other water systems across the country in multi-district litigation (MDL) seeking to hold PFAS manufacturers financially responsible for costs related to these compounds. Under the company's PFAS Litigation Universal Surcredit, or PLUS tariff, approved by the Iowa Utilities Commission, eligible settlement proceeds are returned to customers through one-time bill credits after legal expenses are deducted.

This is the latest in a series of PFAS settlement distributions to Iowa American Water customers. The company previously distributed approximately $738,000 in November 2025, approximately $2.19 million in early 2026 and approximately $657,000 in August 2026. With this latest distribution, Iowa American Water will have returned approximately $4.25 million in PFAS settlement proceeds to eligible customers, totaling approx. $62.59 to each qualifying customer account holder.

The bill credit is not based on whether PFAS has been detected in a customer's water supply. Iowa American Water remains committed to meeting all state and federal drinking water standards while proactively addressing evolving PFAS regulations.

PFAS are a group of manufactured chemicals that have been used in consumer products and industrial applications for decades. American Water, along with numerous other water utilities nationwide, participated in MDL proceedings seeking damages from manufacturers of PFAS chemicals. Settlement agreements provide payments over multiple years, allowing utilities to return proceeds to customers as funds are received.

Customers interested in learning more about PFAS and Iowa American Water's water quality efforts can visit iowaamwater.com. Customers can also view annual Water Quality Reports for their local community, which provide detailed information about drinking water quality, testing and compliance with state and federal standards.

TORONTO, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- i-80 GOLD CORP. (NYSE: IAUX) (TSX: IAU) ("i-80 Gold", or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has mined its first gold and commenced production mining on schedule at its Archimedes underground project ("Archimedes" or the "Project"). Archimedes is a high-grade gold project located on the Company's Ruby Hill property within the Battle Mountain-Eureka gold trend in Nevada, USA. It is the Company's second underground mine to come online.

"The start of production mining at Archimedes marks another significant step for i-80 Gold, further strengthening our track record of delivering on key development milestones," stated Paul Chawrun, Executive Vice President & Chief Operating Officer. "We are currently mining oxide and sulfide material at the Project. The oxide material is being placed on the active heap leach pad on the Ruby Hill property, while the sulfide material is being stockpiled for processing at our Lone Tree Plant next year. Our strong technical and operating teams and our underground mining contractor have enabled us to deliver on this milestone safely, on time and largely on budget."

Mr. Chawrun added, "Our focus for the Project now turns to ramping up mining rates through 2027 and stockpiling the refractory material mined in preparation for the commissioning of the Lone Tree Plant late in the year as Archimedes will be a key source of high-grade refractory material feed. Once the Lone Tree Plant is commissioned, we are targeting consolidated annual gold production of 150,000 to 200,000 ounces beginning in 2028 from the Archimedes and Granite Creek underground projects."(1) 

Project Development

Production mining commenced following the scheduled completion of the surface and underground infrastructure required to begin production mining, including ventilation and escape raises. Lateral development to date totals approximately 3,600 meters. Ground conditions remain favorable, and the underground contractor continues to exceed planned productivity rates within the Project's upper 426 Zone. Construction of additional surface and underground infrastructure, such as additional ventilation raises, a permanent mine dry, and offices, will continue through 2027 to support the ramp up to planned mining rates. 

Project construction commenced in September 2025 and has progressed largely in line with the capital development estimate in the March 2025 preliminary economic assessment (the "PEA"),(2) apart from the decision to expand and upgrade surface infrastructure to support the scale of future operations. Upon anticipated completion of the additional surface and underground infrastructure in 2027, total project capital is expected to be approximately $10 million higher than the $47.3 million estimated in the PEA.

Processing and Stockpiling 

Archimedes is a high-grade gold project consisting of sulfide (refractory) mineralized material as well as oxide mineralized material predominately in the upper 426 Zone. The recently completed 2025-2026 drilling program for the upper 426 Zone intersected significant intervals of oxide mineralization outside the mineral resource estimate contained in the PEA (refer to the Company's press release dated June 25, 2026). Metallurgical test work results have confirmed that the oxide material is amenable to heap leaching on the Ruby Hill property at lower overall processing costs compared to processing through the Company's oxide mill circuit at the Lone Tree Plant.

Beginning in mid-November, oxide material mined from the upper 426 Zone was placed on the existing heap leach pad on the Ruby Hill property, and the Company expects to begin recovering the associated gold in the first quarter of 2027.

Mining development rates at Archimedes are progressing faster than outlined in the PEA and moreover, the Company expects the majority of the mineralized material mined in 2027 to be oxide and to be placed on the existing heap leach pad. While the PEA assumed some tonnage being placed on the leach pad in 2027, the majority of the mineralized material mined was expected to be sulfide and toll milled at a 58% payability factor. Given the Company believes a majority of the mined mineralized material in 2027 to be oxide, it is expected that the Company will be able to increase its heap leach production outlook.(3) Full guidance will be provided early in the new year.

As previously disclosed, in 2027 the Company expects to stockpile all refractory material mined at Archimedes, along with a large portion of oxide and refractory material mined at Granite Creek underground. The stockpiled material is intended to be processed at the Company's wholly owned Lone Tree Plant upon its planned commissioning in the fourth quarter of 2027, rather than processed at a third-party facility. Additionally, over the next three years a significant portion of mineralized material mined at the Project is expected to be oxide and placed on the Ruby Hill leach pad.

2027 Planned Feasibility Study

Drilling in the upper 426 Zone was completed in April 2026. Drilling in the lower 426 and Ruby Deeps zones commenced in the second quarter of 2026. Seven underground drill rigs are currently active on site targeting approximately 55,000 meters planned across 140 drill holes. The drilling campaign is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2027 and is designed to evaluate extensions to the mineralized system and enhance resource definition to support the Archimedes feasibility study, which is planned for completion in the second half of 2027.(2)

As of December 31, 2025, Archimedes hosts an Indicated Mineral Resource of 1.8 million tonnes containing 436,000 ounces of gold grading 7.6 grams per tonne and an Inferred Mineral Resource of 4.2 million tonnes containing 988,000 ounces of gold grading 7.3 grams per tonne.(4) The majority of the current Mineral Resource Estimate is hosted in the Ruby Deeps Zone, located below the 5,100-foot elevation of the deposit as demonstrated in the Figure below.
